chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Amr ibn Uthman, from al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the Words of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: 'And it will be said: Who is a caster (of spells)?' and he thinks it is the separation.
For that is the son of Adam when death comes upon him; he says, 'Is there a physician?'
He is convinced of the separation from his loved ones.
And the calf binds to the calf; the world binds to the Hereafter.
Then to your Lord on that day is the driving.
He said: The return is to the Lord of the worlds.

key_terms.السَّاقُ: Calf (of the leg), used metaphorically for the world or the body
key_terms.الْفِرَاقُ: Separation (of soul from body or loved ones)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'the calf binding to the calf' in Surah Al-Qari'ah according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) elucidates the verses of Surah Al-Qari'ah by linking the dying person's search for a healer to the inevitable separation from loved ones, while interpreting the 'binding of calf to calf' as the world clinging to the Hereafter. This exegesis highlights the transition from worldly attachment to the final return to the Lord, emphasizing the spiritual reality of death as a decisive shift in existence.
